cohort: The study included 67,301 pregnancies from women who gave birth at a tertiary center in Thailand between 1992 and 2022, comparing 121 women aged >= 45 years with 51,315 women aged 20-34 years.
finding: Maternal age >= 45 years is an independent risk factor for markedly higher rates of fetal trisomy, preterm birth, low birth weight, fetal growth restriction, preeclampsia, and other adverse pregnancy outcomes compared to women aged 20-34 years.
mod_finding: The rate of cesarean section was significantly higher in women aged >= 45 years.
